open_obligations: Check that book summarisation is beyond what a single human could evaluate in the relevant sense.
Note that only about 5% of summaries match human quality, so the demonstration is partial.
Confirm that Wu et al. use human feedback at every level rather than only at leaves.
in.other_title: Recursive task decomposition plus human feedback for summarizing entire books
in.rationale: Christiano et al. leave open whether Iterated Amplification can be applied to complex real-world tasks. Wu et al. combine human feedback with recursive task decomposition to summarise whole books, report labelers could supervise without reading whole books, and find summaries match human quality in about 5% of books; the decomposition is fixed chunking rather than learned, and the task is not beyond human scale.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether recursive decomposition with human feedback can be applied to real tasks humans cannot easily evaluate directly, for whole-book summarisation

text: The authors pose as future work removing their simplifications to test whether Iterated Amplification can be usefully applied to complex real-world tasks for which no other training strategy is available. In the discussion they leave a convincing demonstration on beyond-human-scale tasks to future work.
title: Can Iterated Amplification be applied to complex real-world beyond-human-scale tasks?
